subject.title: feat: allow standalone MCP Apps to use bound tools and resources

question: Should OpenClaw permit a ticketed standalone MCP App host to invoke the owning server’s App-visible tools and resources under this view-bound authorization model?
rationale: The patch can be technically sound while still establishing a durable browser authority boundary and new standalone capability that protected-label workflow requires maintainers to accept explicitly.

options.title: Approve the scoped bridge
options.body: Accept the capability after a current-main rebase and rerun of the focused gateway and Chromium security-boundary proof.

options.title: Keep standalone views read-only
options.body: Reject the new authority surface and retain the existing ticketed renderer until a narrower product design is selected.

options.title: Narrow the capability first
options.body: Allow only a subset such as resource reads or explicitly selected tool classes, then request updated authorization and browser proof.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the capability after a current-main rebase and rerun of the focused gateway and Chromium security-boundary proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged and proposed MCP App boundary work makes this person the clearest available technical routing contact; final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
